about: A very fast code counter that reports lines of code, comments and complexity for many languages.

prs.title: PowerShell files count comments correctly around single quotes
prs.broken: Single-quoted PowerShell strings were not understood, so a quote mark inside one started a fake string or comment. Real scripts came out with wrong code and comment counts.
prs.changed: Single-quoted strings and here-strings are now read as strings, so what is inside them can't start anything else.
prs.matters: People measuring PowerShell projects get the real number of code and comment lines.

prs.title: A quote character in OCaml and Nim no longer swallows comments
prs.broken: In OCaml and Nim, a quote written as a single character opened a string that ran on to the next quote, so comments in between counted as code.
prs.changed: That character form is now recognised and closes right away. Type variables and number suffixes that start with an apostrophe are left alone.
prs.matters: OCaml and Nim files report the correct split of code and comments.

prs.title: Elixir character literals no longer swallow comments
prs.broken: Elixir writes a character's code as a question mark before it. A quote written that way opened a string, so comments up to the next quote counted as code.
prs.changed: Those forms now count as plain code, since a question mark before a quote means nothing else in Elixir.
prs.matters: Elixir code that parses strings gets correct comment and code counts.
